source_evidence.anchor: Section 2.1, Floating-point numbers and rounding to nearest, and equations (2.1a)-(2.1b)
source_evidence.observation: The standing model uses a set F of finite floating-point numbers with radix beta, precision p, and exponent range; fl rounds to nearest with arbitrary tie-breaking, and the unit roundoff is u = (1/2) beta^(1-p). Underflow and overflow are defined exceptional events.

The improved bounds are stated to hold, provided underflow and overflow do not occur, for any radix, tie-breaking rule, dimension, and evaluation order of the sums, without quadratic terms in u or a dimension restriction.
The paper defines a_ij as the (i,j) entry of A and diag(f(i)) as the n by n diagonal matrix with diagonal entries f(i), with i implicitly ranging from 1 through n.

For floating-point evaluation of c minus a sum of k-1 products, followed optionally by division by a nonzero floating-point b_k, Lemma 4.1 gives coefficient bounds (k-1)u without division and ku with division, for any evaluation order and in the absence of underflow and overflow.

For A in F^(m x n), m >= n, completed Gaussian elimination produces L_hat in F^(m x n) and U_hat in F^(n x n) satisfying L_hat U_hat = A + DeltaA and |DeltaA| <= n u |L_hat||U_hat|. When m = n, the theorem additionally gives |DeltaA| <= diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat| <= (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|.

The proof analyzes Doolittle's formulation: the k-th U row is computed from an unscaled residual, the k-th L column from a residual divided by the computed pivot U_hat_kk, and L_hat_kk is set to 1. The resulting local residual coefficients are (k-1)u for U-row entries and ku for below-diagonal L-column entries.

source_evidence.anchor: Final coefficient comparison in the proof of Theorem 4.2
source_evidence.observation: The general bound follows from k <= n. In the square case, for the below-diagonal entry with row index i > k, ku <= (i-1)u <= (n-1)u, yielding the rowwise diagonal bound and then the uniform (n-1)u bound.

binders: The matrix dimensions are m and n with m >= n; their positive-integral status is implicit in their use as matrix dimensions and in the Doolittle loop k = 1,...,n. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]
A is a given matrix in F^(m x n). [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
L_hat in F^(m x n) and U_hat in F^(n x n) are the computed factors. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
DeltaA has shape m x n and is fixed by the exact mathematical identity L_hat U_hat = A + DeltaA. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
F and u inherit the standing floating-point definitions, with u = (1/2) beta^(1-p). [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1 and equations (2.1a)-(2.1b)]
hypotheses: The input entries are finite floating-point numbers because A belongs to F^(m x n). [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1]
Gaussian elimination runs to completion. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
Underflow and overflow do not occur during the floating-point computation. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
The sharper rowwise and uniform bounds require the additional hypothesis m = n. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2)]
conclusions: The computed factors obey the exact backward-error identity L_hat U_hat = A + DeltaA and the general rectangular componentwise bound |DeltaA| <= n u |L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

If m = n, then |DeltaA| <= diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat|, where the diagonal factor acts on rows. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2); PDF p. 9 (printed p. 692), matrix-index and diag convention]
If m = n, the rowwise estimate further implies |DeltaA| <= (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2)]
definitions_and_conventions: The hat notation identifies computed quantities; A remains the given floating-point input, while L_hat and U_hat contain the computed factor entries. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]

The identity defining DeltaA is an exact mathematical identity involving the exact product of the stored computed factors, not another rounded matrix multiplication. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

The notation a_ij means the (i,j) matrix entry, and diag(f(i)) is the n by n diagonal matrix whose i-th diagonal entry is f(i), with i = 1,...,n. [PDF p. 9 (printed p. 692), notation paragraph before Section 4.1]

In the Doolittle normalization used by the proof, L_hat_kk = 1. The index ranges make L_hat lower trapezoidal and U_hat upper triangular, although Theorem 4.2 itself states only their dimensions and calls them factors. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]
implicit_context: No explicit rank or nonsingularity hypothesis is stated; the operative condition is that Gaussian elimination runs to completion. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
The shape of DeltaA is implicit from L_hat U_hat = A + DeltaA rather than separately declared. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

The nearby passage does not separately define matrix absolute value or matrix inequality; their entrywise interpretation is inherited from the scalar residual inequalities (4.3a)-(4.3b) used to derive the matrix bound. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) and the following paragraph]
The sharper diagonal estimate is stated only for square matrices and must not be extended to m > n solely from the displayed theorem. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Section 4.2 presents the result for Gaussian elimination variants, while the proof uses a mathematically equivalent Doolittle formulation. For k = 1,...,n it evaluates y_kj = a_kj - sum_(r=1)^(k-1) L_hat_kr U_hat_rj for j = k,...,n and y_ik = (a_ik - sum_(r=1)^(k-1) L_hat_ir U_hat_rk)/U_hat_kk for i = k+1,...,m; U_hat_kk is the computed y_kk, U_hat_kj and L_hat_ik are the corresponding computed outputs, and L_hat_kk = 1. Lemma 4.1 applies whatever the summation order. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Section 4.2 and Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]
numerical_model: F is a symmetric set of finite floating-point numbers, similar to IEEE 754-2008, with radix beta >= 2, precision p >= 1, an exponent range, and zero included. [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1]
The rounding function fl rounds real values to nearest, with no fixed tie-breaking rule, whenever overflow does not occur. [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1]

The unit roundoff is u = (1/2) beta^(1-p), and the standard relative-error models have error magnitude at most u when neither underflow nor overflow occurs. [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), equations (2.1a)-(2.1b)]
The LU analysis permits any evaluation order for the sums in the Doolittle expressions. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]

The improved result is asserted for any radix, tie-breaking rule, dimension, and evaluation order, conditional on absence of underflow and overflow. [PDF p. 4 (printed p. 687), paragraph following equation (1.8)]
error_notions: DeltaA is a backward error on the input matrix: the computed factors exactly factor A + DeltaA. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

The bounds are componentwise absolute backward-error bounds scaled by the ordinary matrix product |L_hat||U_hat|, rather than forward-error bounds on either factor. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]

The local residual for an entry of the computed U row has coefficient (k-1)u, while the local residual for an entry obtained through the computed L column and pivot division has coefficient ku. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]
norms: No vector or matrix norm occurs in Theorem 4.2 or equation (4.2). The absolute values and inequalities have an entrywise interpretation, as shown by the scalar residual bounds assembled into the matrix estimate. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2 and equation (4.2); PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]
constants_and_indexing: The general rectangular coefficient is exactly n u, where n is the column count and inner factor dimension; it is not m u or (n-1)u. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

For square matrices, row i has coefficient (i-1)u, with i running from 1 to n; hence the first row coefficient is zero. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2); PDF p. 9 (printed p. 692), diag convention]
The square uniform coefficient is exactly (n-1)u. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2)]
Equation (4.3a) uses coefficient (k-1)u for j = k,...,n, while equation (4.3b) uses coefficient ku for i = k+1,...,m. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]

The rowwise square coefficient follows because a below-diagonal entry has i > k, so ku <= (i-1)u <= (n-1)u; the other local coefficient is already (k-1)u for row k. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), final coefficient comparison]
higher_order_terms: The coefficients n u, (i-1)u, and (n-1)u are stated without gamma factors, denominators, or omitted O(u^2) terms. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2 and equation (4.2)]
The paper explicitly characterizes the improved bounds as O(u^2)-free and unrestricted by conditions such as n u < 1. [PDF p. 4 (printed p. 687), paragraphs following equation (1.8)]
exceptional_values: Underflow and overflow are excluded. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
The input matrix contains finite floating-point values; infinities and NaNs are not members of the stated set F. [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

Zero entries are permitted because F contains zero, but the Doolittle proof divides by U_hat_kk; the source handles unusable pivots through the condition that Gaussian elimination runs to completion rather than by an explicit nonzero-pivot or nonsingularity hypothesis. [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]

Underflow follows the paper's stated convention: it occurs when rounding an inexact result in the subnormal range; multiplication and division can underflow, whereas floating-point addition cannot under this convention. [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1]

undebatable_constraints: A must have dimensions m x n with m >= n, L_hat must have dimensions m x n, and U_hat must have dimensions n x n. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
The result is conditional on Gaussian elimination running to completion and on absence of underflow and overflow. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
The backward-error identity is L_hat U_hat = A + DeltaA. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
The general bound is |DeltaA| <= n u |L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
Both sharper bounds require m = n. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2)]
The sharp rowwise bound is |DeltaA| <= diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat| with i = 1,...,n. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2); PDF p. 9 (printed p. 692), diag convention]
The sharp uniform square bound is |DeltaA| <= (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2)]

The bounds are componentwise and use the computed factors inside |L_hat||U_hat|; they are not normwise bounds and do not use exact, uncomputed LU factors. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]
The local coefficients responsible for the result are (k-1)u for U-row residuals and ku for below-diagonal L-column residuals. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]
No O(u^2) remainder, gamma factor, or condition n u < 1 belongs in the claimed bounds. [PDF p. 4 (printed p. 687), paragraph following equation (1.8); PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

ambiguities.issue: The scope of the phrase "any variant of Gaussian elimination" is not fully enumerated; the proof discusses mathematically equivalent formulations and chooses Doolittle's method. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Section 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), opening of the proof]
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem contains no permutation matrix, while the proof writes the factorization directly against A and analyzes unpermuted Doolittle formulas. Pivoting conventions are not discussed in this passage. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]
ambiguities.impact: The claim should not be silently generalized to arbitrary pivoting as L_hat U_hat = A + DeltaA; a pivoted formulation would require clarification of whether A has already been permuted or whether a permutation matrix must appear. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]

ambiguities.issue: The phrase "runs to completion" is not formally defined in the selected passage. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2]
ambiguities.evidence: The analyzed Doolittle recurrence divides by the computed pivot U_hat_kk, but the theorem supplies no separate nonzero-pivot, rank, or nonsingularity hypothesis. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization may represent completion directly or unpack it into valid nonzero divisions, but it must not replace it with an unsupported global nonsingularity assumption without recording that interpretation. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]

ambiguities.issue: The surrounding passage does not explicitly define matrix absolute value and inequality notation. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2 and equation (4.2)]
ambiguities.evidence: The proof derives scalar absolute residual inequalities entry by entry in (4.3a)-(4.3b) and then states the matrix inequality, making the componentwise interpretation clear. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) and following paragraph]
ambiguities.impact: The bars must not be translated as a matrix norm; they denote entrywise absolute values, followed by ordinary matrix multiplication and an entrywise comparison. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) and following paragraph]

ambiguities.issue: The passage specifies standard floating-point evaluation and arbitrary summation order but does not discuss fused multiply-add evaluation. [PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]
ambiguities.evidence: The derivation invokes Lemma 4.1 for floating-point evaluation of products, sums, and a possible division, with the sum represented by an arbitrary evaluation order; no fused-operation variant is identified. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]
ambiguities.impact: A contract should preserve the paper's operation model and should not claim explicit coverage of FMA-based implementations without an additional argument. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), Doolittle formulas]

contract_plain_english: Given an m by n floating-point matrix A with m at least n, suppose Gaussian elimination finishes and no underflow or overflow occurs. Its computed factors L_hat and U_hat exactly factor a nearby matrix A + DeltaA, with componentwise backward error bounded by n u times |L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), Theorem 4.2] When A is square, row i has the sharper coefficient (i-1)u, so |DeltaA| is bounded by diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat| and hence by (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10 (printed p. 693), equation (4.2); PDF p. 9 (printed p. 692), diag convention] The proof obtains the exact offsets from Doolittle residuals with coefficients (k-1)u for computed U-row entries and ku for computed below-diagonal L-column entries, using k <= i-1 in the square case. [PDF p. 11 (printed p. 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) and final coefficient comparison] These are componentwise, O(u^2)-free bounds with no condition such as n u < 1, under the paper's round-to-nearest model with arbitrary tie-breaking and summation order. [PDF p. 4 (printed p. 687), paragraph following equation (1.8); PDF p. 5 (printed p. 688), Section 2.1]
